events.title: Chateau Lantern Tours
events.description:
Step into history and mystery at the Chateau de Morès State Historic Site in Medora during the Chateau Lantern Tours. Explore the darker side of the Chateau's past in a thrilling evening of frights, delights, and minimal lights.

The one-hour tours are offered Oct. 23 and 24 at 6:30, 7, 7:30, 8, and 8:30 p.m.

After an introduction at the Interpretive Center, walk to the Chateau for a tour through the main level and upstairs. While venturing through the Chateau, illuminated by lanterns, hear tales of apparitions, ghost lights, murder, and more. Although nothing will jump out to frighten you, you never know what will be around the next corner.

Tickets are $10 for adults and $5 for ages 6 to 17 and can be purchased in advance to ensure a reserved spot by calling 701.623.4355 or visiting the Chateau de Morès Interpretive Center. Lanterns will be provided. Guests should dress warmly with the weather in mind. The Chateau de Morès is a historic home with narrow stairs, uneven floors, and other accessibility concerns.

This event is part of the ND250 commemoration celebrating our country’s 250th birthday.

For more information, contact Outreach Coordinator Shelby Reidle, shschateau@nd.gov or 701.623.4355. The Chateau de Morès State Historic Site is managed by the State Historical Society of North Dakota. The Chateau de Morès Interpretive Center and home are open daily from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. through Sept. 30. Beginning Oct. 1, the Chateau de Morès Interpretive Center will be open Tuesday-Saturday, 9 a.m.-5 p.m., and closed Sunday-Monday.

events.title: Books and Banter: "The Raven"
events.description:
“Books and Banter,” a monthly book club featuring Victorian-era literature, will meet Tuesday, Oct. 20, 9-10 a.m. at the Chateau de Morès Interpretive Center in Medora. Book selections are intended to be easy to read and fun to discuss. Coffee and tea will be provided.

This month's book, “The Raven” by Edgar Allan Poe, is available to read for free via Project Gutenberg. In addition to getting in the spooky spirit, the discussion will touch on Poe's place in American literature and memorable lines from his poetry and prose.

When the State Historical Society of North Dakota took possession of the Chateau de Morès, it held a library so extensive that locals would borrow its books. The subjects of these books range from poems to military tactics, early childhood education to romance novels, and animal husbandry to human medical care.

This event is part of the ND250 commemoration celebrating our country’s 250th birthday.
